name: Kerr parametric oscillator, 27 stored photons
question: Which of its two states does a Kerr parametric oscillator choose when its two-photon drive is swept through threshold with a weak one-photon bias, and with what probability?
assumptions: Frame rotating at half the pump frequency; hbar = 1; rates in units of the single-photon loss kappa.
Single-photon loss only; the two-photon drive is ramped linearly from zero and then held.
The stored states hold about 27 photons at the end of the ramp; the truncation at 69 quanta leaves their Fock tails below 1e-8.
The bias is set so that the Gaussian-stage law predicts a probability of 0.75 for the favoured state.

provenance.reference: Kerr parametric oscillators of H. Goto, Sci. Rep. 6, 21686 (2016) and N. E. Frattini et al., Phys. Rev. X 14, 031040 (2024); the selection law of D. K. Kondepudi and G. W. Nelson, Nature 314, 438 (1985); the bias-probability relation of A. Gu et al., Phys. Rev. Research 7, L022056 (2025)
